A Nigerian scholar on research for doctorate degree at Manchester University, Adewunmi Rachael Mbang has won the 2026 edition of “November to Remember” research competition on Artificial Intelligence organized by the institution. Mbang ; a daughter-in-law of former President of Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and former president of Methodist Church, Nigeria late prelate Sunday Mbang emerged the winner beating other candidates in the competition. The scholar, who also serves as the doctoral representative of the British Academy of Management United Kingdom, was also the Panel Moderator in other events scheduled for the “November to Remember” programme. Speaking with Journalists on Tuesday in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, Mbang said the event was held on the theme, “Intelligent Futures : AI, Innovation and Human Flourishing” brought together scholars, innovators and leaders to discuss how Artificial Intelligence and innovation can be used to improve human life. She said, “My presence and leadership at the panel further highlighted the growing contribution of Nigerians in global conversations on AI, research and innovation. I was a cynosure of all eyes and many admired my contributions and I was rated as the best in all the presentations “ Nigeria urged to adopt UAE model for AI accountability Bayelsa seeks Lagos expertise on AI pricing, e-procurement Police deny declaring man wanted for impregnating eight women in Cross River Mbang recounted her journey, urging every youth to advance themselves in the areas of science and technology. ”The trophy is not only for me. I dedicate it to Nigeria so that the world would know that we are contributing to knowledge in science and technological developments. Our youths should advance themselves particularly in the areas of science and technology”, she said. Emem Julius
